message: 747 posts is a solid content library — clearly you've been consistent in the Miami market. Curious what drives most of your business there: rental for events and venues, or more permanent install work? Florida's event scene seems like it could push both directions pretty hard.

Rental in Miami is a solid market — events, Art Basel, corporate gigs all year. What are you typically deploying for indoor stages? Curious if you're running something like P3.91 or going finer pitch for closer viewing. Always interested in how rental operators in different cities spec their setups.

Noticed you're doing both indoor fine-pitch walls and outdoor LED across North America — broader range than most AV distributors we come across. We're a Shenzhen-based panel supplier, mostly P1.5–2.5 for corporate installs and control rooms. Always curious what's actually pulling demand on the North American side right now. Is the fine-pitch indoor business growing for you, or are you seeing more traction on the outdoor fixed side?

Saw you're running both event rentals and fixed outdoor advertising — that's a wide range to be sourcing for. I'm on the supply side out of Shenzhen, been paying attention to what's moving in Latin America lately. What's the split like for you — more rental panels for events, or permanent installs? And what pixel pitch range do you work with most?

Fifteen years running display projects in Colombia, with Samsung on one side and LED video walls on the other — that's an interesting position to be in, especially as fine pitch keeps pushing into spaces that used to be LCD territory.

What pixel pitch are you seeing most demand for in Bogotá lately — still mostly P2.5 and above, or are clients starting to ask for sub-2mm?

Saw you're both making and distributing screens across Colombia — that's a different supply chain position than most. For the events side of the business, are you running your own rental fleet or supplying panels to AV companies? I've been curious how altitude affects panel specs in Bogotá — 2,600m really changes heat dissipation expectations. What pixel pitch moves best in your market?

Noticed your setup covers both rental events and media facades in Medellín — two pretty different animals to manage on the same team. Facades demand long-term color consistency across fixed installs; rental is all about fast rigging and surviving the road. What cabinet system are you running for events — aluminum or carbon fiber? And what pitch are your panels?

Running 24-hour rental service across an entire country is no small operation — especially when something goes down mid-event at 3am. I'm in Shenzhen, working with rental companies on P2.6 and P3.91 setups.

For the large format screens you're deploying at events — are you running aluminum or carbon fiber cabinets? Curious how they hold up in the Colombian climate.

AV integration with LED video walls is an interesting position — you cover both the display and the integration layer. What pixel pitch range do you spec most for corporate installs in Canada, and is fine-pitch indoor growing faster than the outdoor work right now?

Covering six cities for events means logistics and quick setup matter as much as specs. What cabinet system are you running for the longer-haul setups — aluminum or carbon fiber? And what screen size do you deploy most for outdoor stages across the region?

Running P5 through P2 across indoor and outdoor is a wide range to source for. The P2 indoor work is usually where specs get most specific — viewing distance, refresh rate, calibration. What is driving most of your P2 inquiries lately — corporate installs, control rooms, or something else?

B Corp certification in the LED industry is rare — real differentiator with ESG-conscious corporate clients. OOH media, rental, and direct panel sales in the same operation is a broad model. What is the main focus right now — rental fleet, fixed outdoor, or indoor fine pitch?

Manufacturing for 20 years and expanding across LatAm puts you in a different position than most regional distributors. Mesh panels are still a niche — curious what applications are driving your mesh inquiries. Building facades, or more temporary event installs?

Concert-grade LED alongside congress and seminar setups means managing very different viewing distances and ambient light in the same fleet. What pixel pitch are you running for the indoor congress work — P2.5 range, or have clients been pushing for tighter?

Stadium LED is its own challenge — camera-capture refresh rates, sun exposure on open stadiums, viewing angles across different seat distances. What specs do Peru stadium projects typically land on? Are you seeing more indoor arena work or open outdoor venues?

3,000+ clients and your own CMS platform is a different business model than most regional LED suppliers — the software layer changes what you can offer. What has been driving the most volume lately — outdoor fixed installs, the mobile units, or indoor? And do you run your own production or mixed supply chain?

Concert and congress setups are about as far apart as two LED applications get — one needs wide viewing angle and high refresh for camera capture, the other needs close-range clarity in controlled light. Curious how you spec for each in your fleet. What pixel pitch are you running for indoor seminar work versus outdoor concert stages?

Rental across Mexico with that kind of coverage means the logistics side is as demanding as the specs. For outdoor stage setups — what cabinet system are you running? Curious whether the operation has moved to carbon fiber to cut transport weight or still running aluminum.

Full-color outdoor advertising panels require very different specs than indoor custom signage — brightness, IP rating, viewing angle all shift significantly. What segment drives more of your volume right now, outdoor fixed installs or custom indoor projects?

Sales and installation under one roof in Colombia means you are on the hook for the full spec decision, not just the sale. What pixel pitch range are you installing most — and is the market pushing toward finer pitch for indoor, or is outdoor fixed still the main volume driver?

Offering 24-month financing on LED screens in Argentina is a smart differentiator — most suppliers just sell. Curious what that does to your product mix: are buyers going for larger formats when financing is available, or more fine-pitch indoor installs?
